alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued October 26 at 3:05AM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
A trough moving over the state should bring abundant tropical
moisture and is expected to remain nearly stationary for a few days.
Heavy rain and isolated thunderstorms are possible, potentially
leading to flooding across all islands.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flood prone roads and other low lying areas may be closed
due to elevated runoff and overflowing streams. Urban areas may
receive more significant flooding and property damage due to rapid
runoff.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
may develop Tuesday and continue through Wednesday evening as a
trough moves over the state.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM HST Mon Oct 26 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of
Manzanillo, Mexico, and on recently downgraded Tropical Depression
Olana, located several hundred miles west-southwest of Johnston
Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Papin
